domain_symbols.measure_space: measurable spaces with sigma-algebras and measures

rules.name: Sigma-algebra definition
rules.input_form: collection of subsets of X
preconditions: The ambient set X is fixed
rules.operation: Recognize a sigma-algebra by empty-set, complement, and countable-union closure.
examples: The Borel sigma-algebra on R is generated by open sets
counterexamples: Closure under only finite unions is insufficient

rules.name: Measure countable additivity rule
rules.input_form: pairwise disjoint measurable sets E_n
preconditions: The sets are measurable and pairwise disjoint
rules.operation: Apply countable additivity of a measure over disjoint measurable sets.
examples: Disjoint interval decompositions add their measure values
counterexamples: Applying countable additivity to overlapping sets without adjustment is invalid

rules.name: Measurable function criterion seed
rules.input_form: function between measurable spaces
rules.output_form: inverse images of measurable target sets are measurable
preconditions: Domain and codomain sigma-algebras are fixed
rules.operation: Test measurability through inverse images of measurable sets.
examples: Continuous real-valued functions on Borel spaces are Borel measurable
counterexamples: Checking only direct images of measurable sets is invalid in general

rules.name: Almost-everywhere equality seed
rules.input_form: functions f and g
rules.output_form: f = g outside a null set
preconditions: A measure and null-set notion are fixed
rules.operation: Identify functions up to measure-zero disagreement in theorem contexts that use almost-everywhere equality.
examples: Changing an integrable function on a null set does not alter its Lebesgue integral
counterexamples: Replacing null-set modification by arbitrary positive-measure modification is invalid

rules.name: Monotone convergence theorem seed
rules.input_form: nonnegative measurable sequence f_n increasing to f
rules.output_form: integral f_n converges upward to integral f
preconditions: The functions are measurable, nonnegative, and increase pointwise to f
rules.operation: Pass limits through integrals for monotone nonnegative sequences.
examples: Simple-function approximations recover integrals through monotone limits
counterexamples: Dropping monotonicity or nonnegativity invalidates the theorem in this form

rules.name: Dominated convergence theorem seed
rules.input_form: f_n converges almost everywhere to f under an integrable dominator g
preconditions: The functions are measurable and satisfy |f_n| <= g with integrable g
rules.operation: Exchange limit and integral under integrable domination.
examples: Dominated convergence upgrades pointwise almost-everywhere convergence to integral convergence under an integrable envelope
counterexamples: Pointwise convergence alone without domination is insufficient in general

rules.name: Fatou lemma seed
rules.input_form: nonnegative measurable sequence with a limit inferior
preconditions: The functions are measurable and nonnegative
rules.operation: Bound the integral of a limit inferior by the limit inferior of the integrals.
examples: Fatou gives one-sided control even when exact limit exchange is unavailable
counterexamples: Applying the lemma without nonnegativity or a compatible lower-bound structure is invalid

rules.name: Fubini-Tonelli seed
rules.input_form: product-space integrand under Tonelli or Fubini hypotheses
preconditions: A product-measure setting and nonnegative or absolute-integrability hypotheses are fixed
rules.operation: Convert product integrals into iterated integrals when the standard hypotheses hold.
examples: Multidimensional integrals can be split into repeated one-dimensional integrations when the theorem hypotheses hold
counterexamples: Reordering arbitrary conditionally integrable expressions without the required hypotheses is invalid

rules.name: Lp space seed
rules.input_form: measurable function with p-th power integrability data
preconditions: A measure space and exponent p >= 1 are fixed
rules.operation: Organize measurable functions by p-th power integrability modulo almost-everywhere equality.
examples: Function comparison can be controlled by normed integrability classes rather than pointwise bounds alone
counterexamples: A measurable function with divergent p-th power integral is not automatically in L^p

rules.name: Caratheodory measurability seed
rules.input_form: outer-measure space with a candidate measurable set
preconditions: An outer measure and splitting criterion are fixed
rules.operation: Construct measurable sets from outer-measure data using the Caratheodory criterion.
examples: Measure can be built from outer-measure data before the final measurable sigma-algebra is fixed explicitly
counterexamples: An arbitrary subset of an outer-measure space is not automatically measurable

rules.name: Radon-Nikodym density seed
rules.input_form: pair of measures with absolute continuity data
rules.output_form: density representation with respect to a base measure
preconditions: Absolute continuity and sigma-finiteness conditions are fixed
rules.operation: Represent an absolutely continuous measure by a density relative to a base measure.
examples: Changing from one measure to another can be expressed through a derivative density instead of recomputing every integral from scratch
counterexamples: Singular measures do not automatically admit Radon-Nikodym densities with respect to the chosen base measure
